h: A column, a chapel and a family with royal connections
p: Gibside was the home of the Bowes family, who made their fortune from coal. Their descendants include the Bowes-Lyon family, so this corner of the Derwent Valley has a link to the late Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother. It adds an extra layer to the story as you wander the grounds.

The estate was laid out in the 1700s as a grand landscape, with a long avenue linking two big set pieces. At one end stands the Column to Liberty, a towering monument topped with a statue, which you can spot from far across the valley. At the other is the Palladian chapel, a beautifully proportioned building that also served as the family mausoleum. Walking between the two gives you a good sense of just how much ambition went into the place.
Along the way, look out for the ruins of the hall, the orangery and the banqueting house, all of which add a romantic, slightly mysterious feel to the woods.
Red kites were reintroduced to the Derwent Valley in the early 2000s, and these big, graceful birds of prey are now a common sight overhead, hence the name of the play area.

Allow at least half a day. Afterwards, Gateshead has plenty to round things off. The Angel of the North stands on a hill by the A1, the BALTIC art gallery and the Millennium Bridge are on the Quayside, and Newcastle's bars and restaurants are just across the Tyne.
